origin.description: Decode a base64-encoded string into binary data. The source can be a string or a connection; the output is either a raw vector or a binary connection.
origin.usage: base64decode(what, output = NULL, file, strict = FALSE)

arguments.name: what
arguments.text: Data to decode: a string, raw vector, or connection. For a character vector, each element is decoded and the bytes are concatenated.

arguments.name: output
arguments.text: If NULL, the result is a raw vector. Otherwise a file name or binary connection to receive the decoded bytes.

arguments.name: file
arguments.text: File name to read as text instead of what. Only one of what and file may be given.

arguments.name: strict
arguments.text: If TRUE, invalid characters, bad padding, and trailing content raise an error. Otherwise invalid characters are skipped and padding may be missing.

origin.value: A raw vector when output is NULL, otherwise the number of bytes written.
origin.example:
x <- charToRaw("the decoded content, otherwise the number of bytes")
y <- base64decode(base64encode(x))
stopifnot(identical(x, y))
enc <- base64encode(1:100, 70)
stopifnot(identical(as.raw(1:100), base64decode(enc)))

translation.description: Decode base64 text into bytes, or write those bytes to a path or binary file object.

arguments.name: what
arguments.text: A string, a list of strings, bytes, or a text file object. None without file is an error. Each list element is decoded separately and the bytes are joined.

arguments.name: output
arguments.text: None returns bytes. A path or binary file object receives the decoded data and the length written is returned.

arguments.name: file
arguments.text: Path read as text instead of what. Mutually exclusive with what.

arguments.name: strict
arguments.text: True enforces alphabet, padding, and no trailing garbage. False skips invalid characters and allows missing padding.

translation.value: Bytes when output is None, otherwise an integer byte count.
translation.example:
from base64enc.base64decode import base64decode
from base64enc.base64encode import base64encode

x = b"the decoded content, otherwise the number of bytes"
y = base64decode(base64encode(x))
assert x == y
enc = base64encode(list(range(1, 101)), 70)
assert bytes(range(1, 101)) == base64decode(enc)
print(list(y))
